There are different types of anaesthesia, including general anaesthesia, regional anaesthesia, and local anaesthesia. General anaesthesia is used when a patient needs to be completely unconscious during surgery, while regional and local anaesthesia are used for specific areas of the body.

During general anaesthesia, a patient is given a combination of drugs that put them into a state of controlled unconsciousness. This allows them to feel no pain or discomfort during the surgery. The anaesthesia is carefully monitored by the surgical team to ensure the patient remains safe and comfortable throughout the procedure.

Regional anaesthesia involves injecting a local anaesthetic around the area of the body that will be operated on. This blocks the sensation of pain in that specific area, allowing the patient to remain awake and alert during the surgery.

Local anaesthesia is used for minor procedures and involves injecting a local anaesthetic directly into the area where the surgery will take place. This numbs the area, so the patient does not feel any pain during the procedure.
